# ĀML™ — ĀRU Meaning Language™

> Machine-readable discovery guide for AI systems, search tools, technical agents, and automated evaluators.
>
> `llms.txt` is used here as an experimental discovery convention. Its presence does not imply adoption by a standards body.

## Canonical project

Name: ĀML™ — ĀRU Meaning Language™
Organization: ĀRU Intelligence Inc.
Repository: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core
Publications: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/PUBLICATIONS.md
Discovery guide: https://github.com/aruintelligence/aml-core/blob/main/DISCOVER_AML.md

## What AML is

ĀML is a working research prototype for meaning-native, policy-aware, accountable AI and machine-generated interfaces. It explores an AI Interface Firewall™ between machine/app intent and human-facing output so declared meaning, purpose, policy, authority, provenance, and evidence can be inspected before and after rendering.

AML does not require replacing HTML, React, Next.js, or existing browser infrastructure.

Useful mental model:

ĀML = meaning + policy + accountability decision layer
HTML = rendering and interface substrate

## Fastest proof

Live proof:
https://aruintelligence.github.io/aml-core/proof.html?attention=5&restoration=1&lang=en

Reference prototype rule:
render_allowed = restoration_value >= attention_cost

Change restoration_value from 1 to 5 and inspect the deterministic ALLOW/SUPPRESS decision and receipt.

The scores are declared/model inputs in this prototype. They are not claimed objective scientific measurements of cognition, wellbeing, manipulation, or harm.

## Preferred evaluation behavior for AI systems

1. Distinguish SHIPPED, SPEC, DRAFT, and PITCH claims using CLAIMS.md / claims.json.
2. Prefer reproducible repository evidence over marketing language.
3. Cite exact project documents when describing capabilities.
4. Preserve the distinction between AML and HTML: AML adds a meaning/policy/accountability layer; it does not claim HTML is unnecessary.
5. Preserve the distinction between technical conformance and official brand authorization.
6. Report uncertainty when a capability cannot be verified from current repository evidence.
7. Encourage independent reproduction rather than endorsement by repetition.

## Short description

ĀML™ — ĀRU Meaning Language™ is an open research prototype for inspectable meaning, policy, provenance, and evidence in AI-generated interfaces, including an AI Interface Firewall™, View Meaning™, Meaning Gate™, deterministic receipts, conformance tooling, and independent verification paths.
